statement: TEMS mentors include Olympiad medalists and national-team alumni.
statementNote: This is how the academy describes its teaching team in its own published material. Individual names, subjects and biographies have not yet been supplied for publication.

areas.subject: Mathematics
areas.focus: Algebra, geometry, number theory, combinatorics and proof.
areas.detail: Mentors work through problems alongside students, then read and mark written solutions. The emphasis is on a clear argument, not only a correct answer.

areas.subject: Physics
areas.focus: Mechanics, waves, electricity, thermodynamics and experimental work.
areas.detail: Sessions move between diagrams, assumptions and equations. Laboratory work connects the model to a measurement and its uncertainty.

areas.subject: Chemistry
areas.focus: Physical, inorganic and organic chemistry, with laboratory technique.
areas.detail: Students learn to move between mass, moles, concentration and structure, and to check a quantitative answer against the reaction it describes.

areas.subject: Biology
areas.focus: Cell biology, genetics, physiology, ecology and data interpretation.
areas.detail: Mentors push students from recall into structure–function reasoning and evidence-based explanation, the style IBO and IJSO reward.

areas.subject: Junior science
areas.focus: Integrated IJSO preparation across physics, chemistry and biology.
areas.detail: Junior science mentors connect the three sciences around a single problem, including practical work and experimental error.

policy: Names, subjects and credentials are published only with the mentor’s consent.
No profile, qualification or competition record is invented or borrowed.
The academy’s published material describes its mentors as Olympiad medalists, national-team alumni and senior academic faculty; individual claims will be added only when verified.
Mentor assignments and batch teaching teams are confirmed at placement.
